Topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Probability

Target audience: University students (Introductory Statistics/Data Science)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability

Lecture lines:
Conditional probability focuses on a specific subset.
We shrink our world to circle B.
Only the overlap matters now.

Planned animations:
Create a rectangle representing sample space, with circles A and B. Color #44AAFF.
Highlight circle B with border color #FFCC00.
Animate sample space box fading out, leaving only circle B.
Place a smaller subset 'A intersect B' inside B. Color #FF5555.
Show P(A|B) as the ratio of area(A intersect B) to area(B).

Section: section_2 — The Concept of Independence

Lecture lines:
Independent events do not influence each other.
Knowing B tells you nothing about A.
Probabilities remain unchanged by new information.

Planned animations:
Display two separate probability tree diagrams on screen. Color #00FF00.
Label top branch P(A), bottom branch P(not A). Color #FFFFFF.
Animate both trees branching independently with same probabilities. Highlight labels.

Section: section_3 — Introduction to Bayes' Theorem

Lecture lines:
Bayes' Theorem lets us update our beliefs.
We combine a prior with new evidence.
This gives us a refined posterior probability.
It is essential for diagnostic testing.
Evidence shifts the probability weight effectively.

Planned animations:
Display formula P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B) in center. Color #FFFFFF.
Represent Prior P(A) as a bar chart. Color #888888.
Introduce Evidence B as a light pulse moving toward Prior bar. Color #FFCC00.
Animate Prior bar changing size to Posterior P(A|B). Color #FF5555.
Add a summary label 'Updated Belief'. Color #FFFFFF.

Section: section_4 — Bayes and Independence: The Critical Link

Lecture lines:
Independence simplifies Bayes' Theorem significantly.
The formula collapses when events are independent.
Independent evidence provides zero information.

Planned animations:
Display Bayes formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B). Color #FFFFFF.
Flash P(A|B) = P(A) to show independence. Color #FF5555.
Animate the Bayes formula fading out while 'Independence' text appears. Color #FFFFFF.

Section: section_5 — Application: The Detective Case

Lecture lines:
Detectives use Bayes to solve cases.
Evidence helps refine suspect probability.
Dependent evidence provides crucial updates.

Planned animations:
Display a silhouette of a detective. Color #44AAFF.
Place evidence icons (footprints) around the detective. Color #FFCC00.
Show the probability bar increasing as evidence is added. Color #FF5555.

        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Elements

        circle_a = Circle(radius=0.8, color="#44AAFF", fill_opacity=0.6).shift(LEFT * 0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.place_in_area(sample_space, "B2", "E5")
        self.place_in_area(circle_a, "C3", "D4")
        self.place_in_area(circle_b, "C4", "D5")
        self.play(FadeIn(sample_space), Create(circle_a), Create(circle_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
